name: UGREEN
author: Netlens
description: Shows a UGREEN NAS (UGOS or UGOS Pro) as a host with its Docker containers as guests: state, image and published ports. UGREEN has no public API: this uses the web API of the UGOS web page itself (port 9443), as documented by the community, so a firmware update can change it. Read-only; the password is encrypted with the NAS' own public key before it is sent. Also fills the Storage page (Netlens 0.4.180).

info.title: Set up a user for Netlens on the UGREEN NAS
info.text: UGREEN publishes no API, so Netlens uses the one the UGOS web page uses (https://<NAS address>:9443). Make a user of its own: in UGOS open Control Panel > Users > Add, name it netlens with a long random password, and give it administrator rights (the Docker list needs them); allow it no shared folders. Keep two-step verification off for this user. UGOS locks an account for a few minutes after wrong passwords, so Netlens stops retrying by itself after a refused login. Leave 'Verify TLS certificate' off while the NAS uses its self-signed certificate.
info.code:
# UGOS: Control Panel > Users > Add
#   Name: netlens   (a long, random password)
#   Role: administrator, no shared folders, no 2-step verification
# In Netlens: address https://<NAS address>:9443, user netlens, that password

config.label: UGREEN NAS systems
config.help: One line per UGREEN NAS: its UGOS address with port 9443 (https://192.168.0.50:9443) and the user name and password of the Netlens user.

config.label: Verify TLS certificate
config.help: Leave this off while the NAS uses its own self-signed certificate.
